panels.title: Bootstrap Phase
panels.description: Live bootstrap phase from spacetraders_daemon_bootstrap_phase (the gauge is one series per phase, 1=active; this folds them to a single ordinal so the phase name and its colour render in one tile). Phase context changes what every other panel on this dashboard means.

panels.title: Home System
panels.description: Headquarters system from players.metadata, falling back to the system holding the most hulls. Every 'beyond home' number on this dashboard is relative to this.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
     cur_era AS (SELECT COALESCE((SELECT era_id FROM eras WHERE closed_at IS NULL ORDER BY era_id DESC LIMIT 1),
                                 (SELECT MAX(era_id) FROM eras)) AS eid),
     home AS (SELECT COALESCE(
                (SELECT split_part(p.metadata->>'headquarters','-',1)||'-'||split_part(p.metadata->>'headquarters','-',2)
                   FROM players p, me WHERE p.id=me.pid AND p.metadata->>'headquarters' IS NOT NULL),
                (SELECT s.system_symbol FROM ships s, me
                  WHERE s.player_id=me.pid AND COALESCE(s.system_symbol,'')<>''
                  GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, 1 LIMIT 1)) AS sys),
     nb AS (SELECT DISTINCT ge.connected_system AS sys
              FROM gate_edges ge, home, cur_era
             WHERE ge.system_symbol=home.sys AND ge.era_id=cur_era.eid
               AND COALESCE(ge.connected_system,'')<>''),
     priced AS (SELECT w.system_symbol AS sys,
                       COUNT(DISTINCT m.waypoint_symbol) AS markets,
                       MAX(m.last_updated) AS last_priced
                  FROM market_data m
                  JOIN waypoints w ON w.waypoint_symbol=m.waypoint_symbol, me
                 WHERE m.player_id=me.pid GROUP BY 1)
SELECT (SELECT sys FROM home) AS "home";

panels.title: Jump-Reachable Neighbours - pricing status
panels.description: Every system one jump from home, ranked so the highest-yield unpriced target sits at the top. 'Markets Known' comes from waypoint traits we have already surveyed, so an UNPRICED row with a high count is a probe that pays for itself immediately. 'Priced Age' is blank where a system has never been priced.

defaults.noValue: No gate edges from home this era - the gate graph has not been read yet

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
     cur_era AS (SELECT COALESCE((SELECT era_id FROM eras WHERE closed_at IS NULL ORDER BY era_id DESC LIMIT 1),
                                 (SELECT MAX(era_id) FROM eras)) AS eid),
     home AS (SELECT COALESCE(
                (SELECT split_part(p.metadata->>'headquarters','-',1)||'-'||split_part(p.metadata->>'headquarters','-',2)
                   FROM players p, me WHERE p.id=me.pid AND p.metadata->>'headquarters' IS NOT NULL),
                (SELECT s.system_symbol FROM ships s, me
                  WHERE s.player_id=me.pid AND COALESCE(s.system_symbol,'')<>''
                  GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, 1 LIMIT 1)) AS sys),
     nb AS (SELECT DISTINCT ge.connected_system AS sys
              FROM gate_edges ge, home, cur_era
             WHERE ge.system_symbol=home.sys AND ge.era_id=cur_era.eid
               AND COALESCE(ge.connected_system,'')<>''),
     priced AS (SELECT w.system_symbol AS sys,
                       COUNT(DISTINCT m.waypoint_symbol) AS markets,
                       MAX(m.last_updated) AS last_priced
                  FROM market_data m
                  JOIN waypoints w ON w.waypoint_symbol=m.waypoint_symbol, me
                 WHERE m.player_id=me.pid GROUP BY 1),
     geo AS (SELECT w.system_symbol AS sys,
                    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE w.traits LIKE '%MARKETPLACE%') AS markets_known,
                    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE w.traits LIKE '%SHIPYARD%')    AS shipyards,
                    COUNT(*) AS waypoints_known
               FROM waypoints w GROUP BY 1),
     posts AS (SELECT sp.system_symbol AS sys, COUNT(*) AS n
                 FROM scout_posts sp, me WHERE sp.player_id=me.pid GROUP BY 1),
     edge AS (SELECT ge.connected_system AS sys, MIN(ge.gate_waypoint) AS gate,
                     bool_or(ge.under_construction) AS uc
                FROM gate_edges ge, home, cur_era
               WHERE ge.system_symbol=home.sys AND ge.era_id=cur_era.eid
                 AND COALESCE(ge.connected_system,'')<>'' GROUP BY 1)
SELECT nb.sys                                     AS "System",
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(priced.markets,0) > 0        THEN 'PRICED'
            WHEN COALESCE(posts.n,0) > 0               THEN 'PROBE POSTED'
            WHEN COALESCE(geo.markets_known,0) > 0     THEN 'UNPRICED'
            ELSE 'UNSURVEYED' END                  AS "State",
       COALESCE(geo.markets_known,0)::int          AS "Markets Known",
       COALESCE(priced.markets,0)::int             AS "Markets Priced",
       COALESCE(geo.shipyards,0)::int              AS "Shipyards",
       COALESCE(geo.waypoints_known,0)::int        AS "Waypoints Known",
       EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - priced.last_priced))::bigint AS "Priced Age",
       CASE WHEN edge.uc THEN 'UNDER CONSTRUCTION' ELSE 'OPEN' END AS "Gate",
       edge.gate                                   AS "Gate Waypoint"
  FROM nb
  LEFT JOIN priced ON priced.sys = nb.sys
  LEFT JOIN geo    ON geo.sys    = nb.sys
  LEFT JOIN posts  ON posts.sys  = nb.sys
  LEFT JOIN edge   ON edge.sys   = nb.sys
 ORDER BY COALESCE(priced.markets,0) ASC, COALESCE(geo.markets_known,0) DESC, nb.sys;

panels.title: Expansion Reach - priced vs reachable
panels.description: The expansion scoreboard over time. The gap between the two lines is unexploited reach; a flat 'systems priced' line means expansion is stalled, not slow. Cumulative from the first time each system was priced this era.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
     cur_era AS (SELECT COALESCE((SELECT era_id FROM eras WHERE closed_at IS NULL ORDER BY era_id DESC LIMIT 1),
                                 (SELECT MAX(era_id) FROM eras)) AS eid),
     home AS (SELECT COALESCE(
                (SELECT split_part(p.metadata->>'headquarters','-',1)||'-'||split_part(p.metadata->>'headquarters','-',2)
                   FROM players p, me WHERE p.id=me.pid AND p.metadata->>'headquarters' IS NOT NULL),
                (SELECT s.system_symbol FROM ships s, me
                  WHERE s.player_id=me.pid AND COALESCE(s.system_symbol,'')<>''
                  GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, 1 LIMIT 1)) AS sys),
     nb AS (SELECT DISTINCT ge.connected_system AS sys
              FROM gate_edges ge, home, cur_era
             WHERE ge.system_symbol=home.sys AND ge.era_id=cur_era.eid
               AND COALESCE(ge.connected_system,'')<>''),
     priced AS (SELECT w.system_symbol AS sys,
                       COUNT(DISTINCT m.waypoint_symbol) AS markets,
                       MAX(m.last_updated) AS last_priced
                  FROM market_data m
                  JOIN waypoints w ON w.waypoint_symbol=m.waypoint_symbol, me
                 WHERE m.player_id=me.pid GROUP BY 1),
     firsts AS (SELECT sys, MIN(last_priced) AS t FROM priced GROUP BY 1),
     buckets AS (SELECT generate_series(date_trunc('hour', $__timeFrom()::timestamptz),
                                        date_trunc('hour', $__timeTo()::timestamptz),
                                        interval '1 hour') AS b)
SELECT b AS "time",
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM firsts WHERE firsts.t <= b)::int AS "systems priced",
       ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nb) + 1)::int                   AS "reachable (home + neighbours)"
  FROM buckets ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Phase Timeline (COLDSTART -> GATE -> EXPANSION)
panels.description: Which bootstrap phase was active when. Each band is named and coloured directly, so a re-entry into an earlier phase (GATE falling back to COLDSTART) is visible as a colour reversal rather than something to decode off an axis. The band ends where bootstrap hands off and exits.

defaults.noValue: no daemon phase samples in range

panels.title: Coordinator Handoff - bootstrap exit & standing crew
panels.description: The phase's defining event: BOOTSTRAP_COORDINATOR reaching COMPLETED is the handoff to the standing crew. Every other row is a coordinator bootstrap launched on its way out - a RUNNING row here is what keeps the fleet working now.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
     cur_era AS (SELECT COALESCE((SELECT era_id FROM eras WHERE closed_at IS NULL ORDER BY era_id DESC LIMIT 1),
                                 (SELECT MAX(era_id) FROM eras)) AS eid),
     home AS (SELECT COALESCE(
                (SELECT split_part(p.metadata->>'headquarters','-',1)||'-'||split_part(p.metadata->>'headquarters','-',2)
                   FROM players p, me WHERE p.id=me.pid AND p.metadata->>'headquarters' IS NOT NULL),
                (SELECT s.system_symbol FROM ships s, me
                  WHERE s.player_id=me.pid AND COALESCE(s.system_symbol,'')<>''
                  GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, 1 LIMIT 1)) AS sys),
     nb AS (SELECT DISTINCT ge.connected_system AS sys
              FROM gate_edges ge, home, cur_era
             WHERE ge.system_symbol=home.sys AND ge.era_id=cur_era.eid
               AND COALESCE(ge.connected_system,'')<>''),
     priced AS (SELECT w.system_symbol AS sys,
                       COUNT(DISTINCT m.waypoint_symbol) AS markets,
                       MAX(m.last_updated) AS last_priced
                  FROM market_data m
                  JOIN waypoints w ON w.waypoint_symbol=m.waypoint_symbol, me
                 WHERE m.player_id=me.pid GROUP BY 1)
SELECT c.container_type AS "Coordinator",
       c.status         AS "Status",
       COALESCE(to_char(c.stopped_at,'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI'),
                to_char(c.started_at,'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI')) AS "Since",
       c.restart_count::int AS "Restarts"
  FROM containers c, me
 WHERE c.player_id = me.pid
   AND (c.container_type LIKE '%COORDINATOR%')
 ORDER BY CASE WHEN c.container_type='BOOTSTRAP_COORDINATOR' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
          c.status, c.container_type;

panels.description: Seconds since the worst-served scout post completed a sweep, live from the daemon. This is sweep cadence, not row age in market_data - trading scans keep last_updated fresh even when the scout itself is overdue. Default post target is 3600s.

panels.description: Slot-level coverage per post kind, counting extra_slots as well as the primary slot. 'Tour Not Running' is a manned slot whose tour container has died - a silent coverage hole.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
     cur_era AS (SELECT COALESCE((SELECT era_id FROM eras WHERE closed_at IS NULL ORDER BY era_id DESC LIMIT 1),
                                 (SELECT MAX(era_id) FROM eras)) AS eid),
     home AS (SELECT COALESCE(
                (SELECT split_part(p.metadata->>'headquarters','-',1)||'-'||split_part(p.metadata->>'headquarters','-',2)
                   FROM players p, me WHERE p.id=me.pid AND p.metadata->>'headquarters' IS NOT NULL),
                (SELECT s.system_symbol FROM ships s, me
                  WHERE s.player_id=me.pid AND COALESCE(s.system_symbol,'')<>''
                  GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, 1 LIMIT 1)) AS sys),
     nb AS (SELECT DISTINCT ge.connected_system AS sys
              FROM gate_edges ge, home, cur_era
             WHERE ge.system_symbol=home.sys AND ge.era_id=cur_era.eid
               AND COALESCE(ge.connected_system,'')<>''),
     priced AS (SELECT w.system_symbol AS sys,
                       COUNT(DISTINCT m.waypoint_symbol) AS markets,
                       MAX(m.last_updated) AS last_priced
                  FROM market_data m
                  JOIN waypoints w ON w.waypoint_symbol=m.waypoint_symbol, me
                 WHERE m.player_id=me.pid GROUP BY 1),
     slots AS (
       SELECT sp.id AS post_id, sp.kind, sp.assigned_hull, sp.tour_container_id,
              sp.reposition_container_id
         FROM scout_posts sp, me WHERE sp.player_id = me.pid
       UNION ALL
       SELECT sp.id, sp.kind, elem->>'assigned_hull', elem->>'tour_container_id',
              elem->>'reposition_container_id'
         FROM scout_posts sp, me, jsonb_array_elements(NULLIF(sp.extra_slots,'')::jsonb) elem
        WHERE sp.player_id = me.pid)
SELECT kind AS "Kind",
       COUNT(*)::int AS "Slots",
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE COALESCE(assigned_hull,'') <> '')::int AS "Manned",
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE COALESCE(assigned_hull,'')=''
                          AND COALESCE(reposition_container_id,'')='')::int AS "Unmanned",
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE COALESCE(assigned_hull,'') <> ''
                          AND COALESCE(tour_container_id,'') <> ''
                          AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM containers c
                                           WHERE c.id = slots.tour_container_id

panels.title: What this dashboard cannot show you (instrumentation gaps)

options.content:
Two decisions that drive expansion are **log-only** today. Nothing on this dashboard infers them, because a fabricated series is worse than an absent one.

**Per-cycle expansion ranking.** The frontier expansion coordinator scores candidate systems every reconcile cycle (frontier hop distance, freshness demand, cap / cooldown / spend-window gates) before deciding whether to buy a probe and where to send it. That ranking is not persisted to Postgres or Prometheus. The probe-economics panels above are the best available **proxy** - they show the *outcome* of each cycle's decision, not the *reasoning*. Follow-up: a `frontier_expansion_decisions_total{action}` counter.

**Per-operation capital budget (sp-ftqgp).** The 60/40 split of deployable capital between trade and construction emits log lines only - there is no gauge for the budget, its utilisation, or a denial. The *Capital Flow* row below is derived honestly from the `transactions` table: it is **realised** capital movement per operation, which is the outcome the budget governs, not the planned split itself. Do not read it as budget adherence. Follow-up bead filed for the gauge.

panels.title: Realised Capital by Operation
panels.description: Where capital actually went this era, straight from the transactions ledger. This is realised flow - it is NOT the sp-ftqgp planned budget, which is log-only. 'construction_supply' running deeply negative while 'contract' carries the surplus is the signature of the gate build.

       COALESCE(SUM(t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.amount > 0), 0)::bigint AS "In",

panels.title: Probe-Backoff Detail
panels.description: Systems whose gate could not be read this era, with backoff tier and age. Empty is the healthy state.

defaults.noValue: No gates in probe-backoff - every known gate edge read cleanly

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ge.system_symbol AS "System",
       ge.attempt_count::int AS "Attempts",
       EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - ge.unreadable_since::timestamptz))::bigint AS "Unreadable For"
  FROM gate_edges ge WHERE ge.era_id = (SELECT COALESCE((SELECT era_id FROM eras WHERE closed_at IS NULL ORDER BY era_id DESC LIMIT 1),(SELECT MAX(era_id) FROM eras))) AND ge.connected_system = ''
 ORDER BY ge.attempt_count DESC, ge.unreadable_since ASC;

panels.title: Gate Graph Frontier - most-connected known systems
panels.description: The best-connected systems in this era's known gate graph, whether or not they are adjacent to home. High edge count plus UNPRICED marks a future hub worth reaching once a first hop lands.

defaults.noValue: No gate edges recorded this era

targets.rawSql:
WITH e AS (
  SELECT ge.system_symbol AS a, ge.connected_system AS b FROM gate_edges ge WHERE ge.era_id = (SELECT COALESCE((SELECT era_id FROM eras WHERE closed_at IS NULL ORDER BY era_id DESC LIMIT 1),(SELECT MAX(era_id) FROM eras)))
     AND COALESCE(ge.system_symbol,'') <> '' AND COALESCE(ge.connected_system,'') <> ''),
     deg AS (SELECT a AS sys, COUNT(*) AS edges FROM e GROUP BY 1),
     me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
     priced AS (SELECT DISTINCT w.system_symbol AS sys
                  FROM market_data m JOIN waypoints w ON w.waypoint_symbol = m.waypoint_symbol, me
                 WHERE m.player_id = me.pid)
SELECT deg.sys AS "System",
       deg.edges::int AS "Gate Edges",
       COALESCE((SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE w.traits LIKE '%MARKETPLACE%')
                   FROM waypoints w WHERE w.system_symbol = deg.sys), 0)::int AS "Markets Known",
       CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM priced WHERE priced.sys = deg.sys)
            THEN 'PRICED' ELSE 'UNPRICED' END AS "State"
  FROM deg ORDER BY deg.edges DESC, deg.sys LIMIT 20;
